frontier.hypothesis: The property that makes the target's 0x5C site emit shift-as-operand-1 from a base-first source is that the sum is consumed directly as a MEM base with two constant offsets, rather than materialised into two pointer variables that are live into the inner loop; spelling the cursor site the same way reaches class C without the flip and without the store-group reorder.
frontier.mechanism: Both sites are `(plus (reload) (shift))` in the same basic-block family and both are written base-first in our source, yet the 0x5C site ties to the shift (target row 89, which our floor already matches) and the cursor site ties to the reload (target row 65, our residual). The only structural difference on the consumer side is that the cursor's sum feeds two `addiu` that create loop-live pointer variables, so the sum's pseudo has two non-MEM uses across a loop boundary rather than two MEM-base uses in straight-line code; that changes which operand carries the REG_DEAD note combine_regs (local-alloc.c:1784-1946) sees, and hence which operand the dest ties to.
frontier.next_probe: Build the cursor block so that the row base is consumed as a MEM base rather than as two live pointers: (a) drop p_6a/p_7e entirely and write the inner loop as `*(s16 *)(rowp + 0x6A + a2*2) = -1; *(s16 *)(rowp + 0x7E + a2*2) = 0;` with `u8 *rowp = D_800A36A0 + t0*10;`, and (b) the same with the inner loop unrolled/rewritten so that rowp's only uses are MEM bases. Both change the inner loop's instruction count, so measure build_insns first and price the delta against the s20 slack devices (device D is +1 insn for +1 row) before scoring. Confirm the tie with a .lreg dump (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_800770B8) before reading the score.

frontier.hypothesis: The second structural difference between the two sites -- addend `t0*2` (an sll of a plain sign-extended register) versus addend `t0*10` (an sll of a plus) -- is what decides the operand order, so respelling the cursor's index so its RTL def is an sll of a plain register reaches class C on the A-first store order.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 canonicalises commutative operands by complexity during combine/expand; a pseudo whose def is a nested plus may be ordered differently from one whose def is a simple shift. s23 proved the t0*4 -> t0*5 -> t0*10 chain is already byte-exact in the floor body, so any respelling must preserve those four rows while changing only the def shape feeding the final add.
frontier.next_probe: Introduce a real s16 row index (`s16 t5 = (s16)(t0 * 5);`) so the cursor's addend is `t5 * 2` -- an sll of a plain sign-extended register, matching the 0x5C site's shape -- and measure build_insns (the extra sll/sra may cost 1-2 insns; price against the s20 slack devices). Read tmp/grind/func_800770B8/dumps/text1b.combine for both sites in the SAME build to see whether the plus-vs-shift def shape is what the canonicalisation keys on before spending more builds.

frontier.hypothesis: Class B's 170-insn collapse can be avoided if p_old's second live range is forced to survive copy propagation by a use the raw pseudo cannot serve, so the target's $s1/$v0 split becomes reachable at 175 instructions.
frontier.mechanism: s17 and s24 both show that every spelling reaching the raw pseudo lets copy propagation delete p_old's second range, removing the copy plus four dependents (175 -> 170). The target keeps both, so in the original source p_old's second range must have a use that is not substitutable by the raw result -- the candidates are a later read of p_old (none survives in our body) or a use inside a region the propagator will not cross.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate every later reader of the new pointer in the function body (the outer loop reads D_800A36A0, not p_old) and test spellings in which ONE of those readers goes through p_old rather than through the global -- e.g. the outer loop's `u8 *base = D_800A36A0;` replaced by `u8 *base = (u8 *)p_old;` in the first iteration only is not expressible, but `*(s32 *)q = ...`-style splits are; measure build_insns first, since any spelling that deletes a reload lands at 174 and any that adds one lands at 176.

judge_constraints: func_800770B8's honest floor stays 5. Do not respell the t0*4->t0*2 identity detour in any form. The dependence may only be reached if it is FORCED by real program structure -- e.g. group A addressed through a cursor genuinely derived from group C's t0*4 pointer, where the derivation has a truthful semantic reading and emits no instruction the target lacks.
